# Caesura

> Keys for agents that cannot act alone. A NEAR contract holds the only keys; one AI seat
> proposes inside a private enclave, a second held-apart seat checks, and an action executes
> only when both agree and the policy passes. Every decision, including every refusal, is
> sealed under one hash the chain carries and anyone can re-derive offline.

A standalone build on NEAR, live on testnet. Built by mages.city at the NEAR Hackathon, 1–14 November 2026.
Repository: https://github.com/mitchuski/caesura (Apache-2.0). Start with its README: the path is "do X, see Y".

## The name and the mark

- A caesura is the break inside a line of verse; here it is the pause between proposing and acting.
- The two seats are the City's pair: the mage (soulbae) proposes, the sword (soulbis) checks.
  In the City's hand: ⚔️ ⊥ ⿻ ⊥ 🧙 — sword, held apart, the pause where the two overlap, held apart, mage.
- The mark is two bars that overlap: mage coral, sword cyan, the overlap violet. The æ in the
  name is a ligature, two letters cast as one glyph and each still itself: that pause set in the name.

## Mechanism

- Gate: a Rust contract (near-sdk-rs) on a sub-account with no full-access key. Policy state
  (per-action cap, per-day cap, allowed receivers, cooldown, pause). Methods: propose, assay,
  commit_root; owner-only set_policy, pause, rotate_seat_key.
- Seats: two function-call access keys on the gate's account, each scoped to one method.
  Proposer = private inference on NEAR AI Cloud (TEE-signed response + attestation).
  Assayer = a different model that receives only the canonical proposal bytes.
- Evidence: one content-addressed bundle per round (proposal, assay, enclave receipts,
  policy snapshot, transaction id) under a root the gate commits. An offline verifier
  re-derives every address, checks the enclave signatures against the attestation, and
  matches the root to the chain.

## Path (do X, see Y)

1. Deploy the gate; set caps; add one scoped key per seat.
2. Agent pays for compute: propose → assay approves → executed → root committed → verifier green.
3. Poisoned tool result: proposer drafts a drain; assayer refuses; chain records `refused`; the refusal is a leaf.
4. Owner pauses from their own key; the pause is a leaf.
5. `node verify.mjs bundles/<round>` re-derives everything.

## The board

https://caesura.mages.city reads every gate listed in gates.json live from NEAR testnet
(get_state, list_proposals, list_roots) and shows rounds, refusals, attacks held and roots.
Gates (owner caesura.testnet): pause.caesura.testnet carries the demonstration rounds, gap.caesura.testnet the gap study. Every round on them was run inside the hackathon window. Deploy your own with tools/deploy.mjs,
run a poisoned round, verify, then register your gate on chain (tools/registry.mjs register; the
registry gates.caesura.testnet keeps it only if you are the owner the gate names) to join the board.

## Links

- Site: https://caesura.mages.city

## The gap, measured (autoresearch board)

Every round names the attack it ran (corpus/index.json; the task object's address is in the
proposal) and the seat pair that ran it (pairs/). board.json folds rounds into a front per
pair (drained must be 0; held, not taken, honest passed, cost of the pause), an attack x pair
matrix, and studies. First study: the gap ladder. --gap N sets what crosses to the second seat:
g0 policy + proposal only; g1 + task (the designed gap); g2 + rationale; g3 + tool results;
g4 + the proposer's full prompt. Points on the curve are rounds on the gate; the board folds
them as they land. Contribute an
attack, a seat pair, a policy, or a point on the curve; rounds land as roots on your gate.

## Keys with weight (hybrid ed25519 + ML-DSA-65 + SLH-DSA; the ceremony)

A key can sign twice: the ed25519 function-call key the gate holds, and a post-quantum key
beside it (composite suites mldsa65-ed25519 and slhdsa-sha2-128s-ed25519: both halves must
verify over one domain-separated, dual-hash pre-hashed message). Three rungs by data
(key-policy leaf): proposer ed25519; assayer ML-DSA-65 + ed25519 (the releasing seat); owner
SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s + ed25519 (hash-based, installs the seat keys, signs rarely). The ceremony
leaf, signed by the owner, names the key policy and the key commitments; a transfer names the
ceremony and keys it leaves and is countersigned by each key it leaves. The verifier walks the
chain of ceremonies and, with --rpc, checks every ed25519 half against the gate and its owner.
The gate verifies the ed25519 half today; in-contract pq verification is the v2 gate (probed:
ML-DSA-65 31 TGas, SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s 18 TGas).
